newsitem.title: GAMBIA: Gambia coup leader has three presidential rivals.
newsitem.headline: Gambia coup leader has three presidential rivals.

text.p: Gambia's 1994 coup leader Colonel Yahya Jammeh has three rivals for the presidency in Thursday's election, during which he is seeking legitimacy through the ballot box.
Following are brief profiles of the four candidates:

YAHYA JAMMEH, colonel retired, and a group of young army officers toppled independence president Sir Dawda Jawara in a bloodless coup in July 1994, accusing him of corruption. A devout Moslem, Jammeh, 31, received some military training in the United States. He survived a counter-coup in which several soldiers died but in response to foreign pressure he dropped a plan to delay elections until 1998. He quit the army in August to run for president after initially saying he was not interested in politics. Before leaving office, he barred the nation's established politicians from the race by banning anyone who had served under Jawara from election. He is standing for the Alliance for Patriotic Reorientation and Reconstruction (APRC) which he set up with fellow members of the armed forces.

OUSAINOU DARBOE, 48, vice-president of the Gambia Bar Association, is standing for the United Democratic Party. A lawyer who has defended cases against both the Jawara and the Jammeh administrations, he has become a focus of support for the banned parties and their leaders. He has accused Jammeh supporters of attacking his supporters and says Jammeh has enlisted the support of the armed forces and the security forces in his campaign for the presidency.
SIDIA JATTA, 51, is contesting the presidency for a second time. The candidate of the small People's Democratic Organisation for Independence and Socialism, he stood against Jawara in 1992.
HAMAT BAH, 37, is running for the National Reconciliation Party. A hotel owner, he was a surprise candidate. He says he stands for democracy and liberal economic policies.
